category: Toolbar tools II - retouch, paint, draw, type and navigate
description: The lower half of the Photoshop toolbar: healing and cloning tools, the brush and eraser families, gradients and fills, the focus and tone tools, the pen and shape tools, the type tools, and the navigation tools. Tools sharing one toolbar slot are cycled with Shift plus the slot letter.

tools.name: Spot Healing Brush Tool
tools.description: One-click blemish removal: click or drag over a spot and Photoshop synthesises a patch from the surrounding pixels, matching texture, lighting and shading automatically. Content-Aware mode is the default and best general choice; Proximity Match and Create Texture are simpler fallbacks. No source point is needed, unlike the Healing Brush.
tools.usage: Toolbar (J). Shift+J cycles the healing family.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Content-Aware, Create Texture or Proximity Match.

parameters.name: Sample All Layers
parameters.description: Lets you heal onto an empty layer, keeping the original pixels untouched.

parameters.name: Brush size
parameters.description: Slightly larger than the blemish works best; adjust with [ and ].

tools.example:
1. Add an empty layer above the photo and tick Sample All Layers.
2. Press J, set Type to Content-Aware.
3. Click each skin blemish with a brush slightly larger than the spot.
tools.notes: For a linear defect (a hair, a cable) drag along it in one stroke rather than clicking repeatedly.

tools.name: Healing Brush Tool
tools.description: Clones from an Alt-clicked source point but blends the copied texture into the destination's colour, tone and luminosity. Use it when the Spot Healing Brush guesses badly and you need to dictate exactly which area supplies the texture - repairing skin near an edge, or a wall next to a window.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+J to cycle). Alt+click to set the source, then paint.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Blend mode for the heal; Replace preserves noise and grain at the stroke edges.

parameters.name: Source
parameters.description: Sampled (the Alt-clicked point) or Pattern.

parameters.name: Aligned
parameters.description: On keeps the source offset fixed relative to the cursor across strokes.

parameters.name: Sample
parameters.description: Current Layer, Current & Below, or All Layers - use Current & Below to heal onto an empty layer.

tools.example:
1. Create an empty layer, set Sample to Current & Below.
2. Alt+click a clean patch of skin near the blemish.
3. Paint over the blemish; the texture comes from the source but the colour from the target.

tools.name: Patch Tool
tools.description: Lasso a region and drag it onto clean pixels (Source mode) or drag clean pixels onto it (Destination mode); Photoshop heals the boundary so the patch blends. Content-Aware mode adds Structure and Color sliders that control how strictly the fill follows existing edges. Best for removing medium-to-large objects such as a litter bin or a skin crease.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+J to cycle).

parameters.name: Patch
parameters.description: Normal (Source/Destination healing) or Content-Aware.

parameters.name: Structure
parameters.description: 1-7 in Content-Aware mode: how closely the fill follows existing image structure.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: 0-10 in Content-Aware mode: how much colour blending is applied.

parameters.name: Transparent
parameters.description: Blends only texture, keeping the destination's transparency - for patching on gradients.

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+J until the Patch tool is active; set Patch to Content-Aware, Structure 4, Color 3.
2. Draw around the object to remove.
3. Drag the selection to a clean area of background and release, then Ctrl+D.

tools.name: Content-Aware Move Tool
tools.description: Selects an object, moves it to a new position and generatively fills the hole it leaves behind, healing both ends of the operation in one gesture. Extend mode duplicates instead of moving, which is handy for lengthening a wall or a row of railings. A transform box lets you scale and rotate before committing.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+J to cycle). Press Enter to commit.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Move (relocate and fill the origin) or Extend (copy and blend).

parameters.name: Structure / Color
parameters.description: Same blend controls as the Content-Aware Patch.

parameters.name: Transform On Drop
parameters.description: Shows scale/rotate handles for the moved content before it is blended.

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+J until Content-Aware Move is active, Mode = Move.
2. Draw around a boat with a little surrounding water.
3. Drag it to the left side of the frame, adjust the handles and press Enter.

tools.name: Red Eye Tool
tools.description: Removes the red pupil reflection caused by direct flash: drag a box over the eye and the saturated red is replaced with neutral dark grey. Pupil Size and Darken Amount control how much of the pupil is affected and how dark the result is.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+J to cycle).

parameters.name: Pupil Size
parameters.description: Percentage of the detected region treated as pupil.

parameters.name: Darken Amount
parameters.description: How dark the corrected pupil becomes.

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+J until the Red Eye tool is active.
2. Drag a small rectangle over each red pupil.
3. If the result looks grey and flat, undo, raise Darken Amount to 60% and retry.
tools.notes: It only treats human red-eye. Animal eyeshine (green/yellow) must be fixed by hand with a brush or a Hue/Saturation layer.

tools.name: Remove Tool
tools.description: Brush loosely over an unwanted object and Photoshop removes it and reconstructs the background, choosing automatically between AI generation and classic content-aware fill. Since Photoshop 25/26 it also offers Find Distractions in the options bar and Contextual Task Bar to clear people, wires and cables across the whole image in one pass. Usually the fastest object removal for complex backgrounds.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+J to cycle, slot J).

parameters.name: Brush size
parameters.description: Set with [ and ]; scribble over the object plus a little of its shadow.

parameters.name: Remove after each stroke
parameters.description: Off lets you paint several areas and remove them together.

parameters.name: Sample all layers
parameters.description: Reads the composite so you can write the result to a new layer.

parameters.name: Find Distractions
parameters.description: Detects and removes people, or wires and cables, across the image automatically.

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+J until the Remove tool is active.
2. Paint over a lamp post, covering its full width.
3. Release - the background is rebuilt. Repeat on any leftovers.
tools.notes: Unlike Generative Fill it does not require a text prompt and (at the time of writing) does not consume generative credits.

tools.name: Brush Tool
tools.description: The core painting tool: applies the foreground colour with the active brush tip, controlled by size, hardness, opacity, flow, smoothing and blend mode, and responsive to pressure and tilt on a tablet. It also paints on layer masks, channels and Quick Masks, which makes it the workhorse of masking and dodging/burning as well as of digital painting.
tools.usage: Toolbar (B). Right-click the canvas for the brush picker; [ and ] change size, Shift+[ / Shift+] change hardness, number keys set opacity.

parameters.name: Size / Hardness
parameters.description: Tip diameter in pixels and edge softness (0-100%).

parameters.name: Opacity / Flow
parameters.description: Maximum stroke strength versus how quickly paint builds up within one stroke.

parameters.name: Smoothing
parameters.description: 0-100% stroke stabilisation, with pull-string and stroke-catch-up modes.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Blend mode of the paint; Behind and Clear are exclusive to painting tools.

parameters.name: Airbrush
parameters.description: Keeps building paint while the cursor is held still.

tools.example:
1. Add a layer mask to a layer, press B and press D then X so the foreground is black.
2. Set Hardness 0, Opacity 100%, Flow 30%.
3. Paint over the areas to hide; paint with white to bring them back.

JSX equivalent (fill a selection with the foreground colour):
app.activeDocument.selection.fill(app.foregroundColor);

tools.name: Pencil Tool
tools.description: Paints hard-edged, aliased strokes with no anti-aliasing at all - each pixel is either fully painted or untouched. Used for pixel art, 1 px UI lines, icon work and painting exact mask edges where a soft brush would leak.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+B to cycle from the Brush).

parameters.name: Auto Erase
parameters.description: Painting over the foreground colour draws with the background colour instead - a classic pixel-art toggle.

tools.example:
1. Zoom to 800%, press Shift+B until the Pencil is active and set size to 1 px.
2. Click to place single pixels; Shift+click to draw a straight aliased line between two points.

tools.name: Color Replacement Tool
tools.description: Paints the foreground hue onto existing pixels while preserving their underlying texture and shading, sampling continuously so it stays inside the colour it started on. Handy for quick recolouring of clothing or props where a full Hue/Saturation mask would be overkill.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+B to cycle).

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Hue, Saturation, Color (default) or Luminosity.

parameters.name: Sampling
parameters.description: Continuous, Once (locks to the first colour clicked) or Background Swatch.

parameters.name: Limits
parameters.description: Discontiguous, Contiguous or Find Edges.

parameters.name: Tolerance
parameters.description: How far from the sampled colour the replacement spreads.

tools.example:
1. Pick the target colour as the foreground.
2. Press Shift+B until the Color Replacement tool is active; Sampling = Once, Limits = Contiguous, Tolerance 30%.
3. Click on the red jumper and paint - it turns blue while keeping its folds.
tools.notes: Destructive. For production work prefer a Hue/Saturation adjustment layer with a mask or a targeted colour range.

tools.name: Mixer Brush Tool
tools.description: A painterly brush that blends the colour already on the canvas with the colour on the brush, simulating wet media. Wet, Load, Mix and Flow control how much canvas paint is picked up, how much reservoir paint is carried and how they mix, so it can smear a photo into an oil painting or blend a digital painting realistically.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+B to cycle).

parameters.name: Wet
parameters.description: How much paint the brush picks up from the canvas.

parameters.name: Load
parameters.description: How much paint the reservoir holds.

parameters.name: Mix
parameters.description: Ratio of canvas paint to reservoir paint.

parameters.name: Clean the brush after each stroke
parameters.description: Empties the reservoir between strokes.

parameters.name: Sample All Layers
parameters.description: Mixes using the composite so you can paint on an empty layer.

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+B until the Mixer Brush is active; choose the "Very Wet, Heavy Mix" preset.
2. Tick Sample All Layers and add an empty layer above the photo.
3. Paint along the subject's contours to smear the photo into brushwork.

tools.name: Clone Stamp Tool
tools.description: Copies pixels exactly from an Alt-clicked source to wherever you paint, with no blending. Preferred over healing when you need literal duplication or when healing smears near edges and high-contrast boundaries. The Clone Source panel adds up to five sources plus offset, scale, rotation and an overlay preview.
tools.usage: Toolbar (S). Alt+click to set the source, then paint. Window > Clone Source for advanced options.

parameters.name: Aligned
parameters.description: On: the source moves with the cursor across strokes. Off: every stroke restarts from the same source point.

parameters.name: Sample
parameters.description: Current Layer, Current & Below, All Layers - use Current & Below to clone onto an empty layer.

parameters.name: Clone Source overlay
parameters.description: Shows a ghost of the source under the cursor so you can align it precisely.

parameters.name: Ignore adjustment layers
parameters.description: Clones the raw pixels rather than the adjusted result.

tools.example:
1. Add an empty layer, set Sample to Current & Below.
2. Press S, Alt+click a clean stretch of brickwork.
3. Paint over the cable crossing the wall; re-sample often to avoid a visible repeating pattern.
tools.notes: For non-destructive work always clone onto an empty layer - you can then erase or mask mistakes without touching the original.

tools.name: Pattern Stamp Tool
tools.description: Paints with a repeating pattern from the pattern presets instead of sampled pixels. Impressionist mode smears the pattern into loose dabs. Used for texture overlays, quick fabric or paper fills and custom brush-driven pattern work.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+S to cycle from the Clone Stamp).

parameters.name: Pattern
parameters.description: Any preset in the Patterns panel, or one defined with Edit > Define Pattern.

parameters.name: Aligned
parameters.description: Keeps the pattern tiles in register across separate strokes.

parameters.name: Impressionist
parameters.description: Paints blurred, smeared dabs of the pattern.

tools.example:
1. Select a rectangle of a paper texture and run Edit > Define Pattern.
2. Press Shift+S until the Pattern Stamp is active and choose the new pattern.
3. Paint the texture over the background on a new layer set to Overlay.

tools.name: History Brush Tool
tools.description: Paints back the image as it existed at a chosen history state or snapshot, letting you undo an effect selectively. The classic use is to apply a filter to the whole image, step back in the History panel, then brush the filtered result in only where it is wanted.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Y). Set the source by clicking the left column of a state or snapshot in the History panel.
tools.example:
1. Run Filter > Blur > Gaussian Blur over the whole layer.
2. In the History panel click the box beside the blurred state to set it as the source, then click the previous (sharp) state.
3. Press Y and paint the blur back in only over the background.
tools.notes: History is per-session and per-document: closing the file clears it, and states are lost once the history limit (Preferences > Performance) is reached.

tools.name: Art History Brush Tool
tools.description: Paints from a history state with stylised, curling strokes (Tight Short, Loose Curl, Dab and other styles), turning a photograph into an impressionistic painting. A niche creative tool rather than a retouching one.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+Y to cycle from the History Brush).

parameters.name: Style
parameters.description: Tight Short/Medium/Long, Loose Medium/Long, Dab, Tight Curl, Loose Curl and so on.

parameters.name: Area
parameters.description: The area each stroke covers - larger values paint more strokes per dab.

parameters.name: Tolerance
parameters.description: Restricts painting to areas that differ from the source; 0 allows painting anywhere.

tools.example:
1. Take a snapshot of the photo in the History panel and set it as the history source.
2. Fill the layer with white, press Shift+Y for the Art History Brush, Style = Tight Curl, Area 50 px.
3. Paint across the canvas to reveal the photo as swirling brushstrokes.

tools.name: Eraser Tool
tools.description: Deletes pixels to transparency on a normal layer, or paints the background colour on a locked Background layer. Modes mirror the Brush, Pencil and Block tips. "Erase to History" restores from the history source instead of erasing.
tools.usage: Toolbar (E). Hold Alt to erase to the history source.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Brush (soft), Pencil (aliased) or Block (fixed square).

parameters.name: Opacity / Flow
parameters.description: Partial erasing strength.

parameters.name: Erase to History
parameters.description: Restores pixels from the selected history state.

tools.example:
1. Press E, Mode = Brush, Opacity 100%.
2. Erase the unwanted corner of a pasted layer.
tools.notes: Erasing is destructive. Prefer a layer mask (Layer > Layer Mask > Reveal All, then paint black) so the pixels can be recovered.

tools.name: Background Eraser Tool
tools.description: Erases the colour sampled under the crosshair while protecting other colours, so it can cut a subject out of a background as you paint along the boundary. Protect Foreground Color shields a chosen colour, and Sampling Once locks the erased colour to the first click.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+E to cycle from the Eraser).

parameters.name: Sampling
parameters.description: Continuous, Once or Background Swatch.

parameters.name: Limits
parameters.description: Discontiguous, Contiguous or Find Edges.

parameters.name: Tolerance
parameters.description: Colour range erased around the sampled colour.

parameters.name: Protect Foreground Color
parameters.description: Never erases pixels matching the foreground swatch.

tools.example:
1. Duplicate the layer (the tool is destructive).
2. Press Shift+E until the Background Eraser is active; Sampling = Once, Limits = Discontiguous, Tolerance 25%.
3. Keep the crosshair on the sky and paint around the tree so only the sky disappears.

tools.name: Magic Eraser Tool
tools.description: One click erases all pixels within a tolerance of the clicked colour, the eraser equivalent of the Magic Wand. Fast for knocking a flat white or single-colour background out of a logo or product shot.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+E to cycle).

parameters.name: Tolerance
parameters.description: Colour distance erased around the clicked pixel.

parameters.name: Contiguous
parameters.description: On: only the connected region. Off: every matching pixel in the layer.

parameters.name: Opacity
parameters.description: Below 100% leaves a partially transparent result.

tools.example:
1. Unlock the Background layer (click the padlock).
2. Press Shift+E until the Magic Eraser is active, Tolerance 20, Contiguous on.
3. Click the white background - it becomes transparent.

tools.name: Gradient Tool
tools.description: Draws a linear, radial, angle, reflected or diamond blend between colours. Since Photoshop 25 the default is a live, editable on-canvas gradient that creates a gradient fill layer with draggable colour stops, while Classic mode in the options bar restores the old drag-to-rasterise behaviour. Gradients are also used constantly on layer masks to fade one layer into another.
tools.usage: Toolbar (G). Drag across the canvas; hold Shift to constrain the angle.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Linear, Radial, Angle, Reflected, Diamond.

parameters.name: Mode / Opacity
parameters.description: Blend mode and opacity applied as the gradient is drawn.

parameters.name: Dither
parameters.description: Adds noise to hide banding in smooth blends.

parameters.name: Reverse / Transparency
parameters.description: Flips the colour order; respects the gradient's alpha stops.

parameters.name: Classic gradient
parameters.description: Switches back to the pre-25 behaviour of painting pixels directly.

tools.example:
1. Add a layer mask to the top layer.
2. Press G, choose Foreground to Transparent, Linear, and press D for black/white.
3. Drag from the bottom of the frame upwards to fade the layer out.

tools.name: Paint Bucket Tool
tools.description: Fills all pixels similar to the clicked one with the foreground colour or a pattern, using the same tolerance/contiguity logic as the Magic Wand. Quickest way to flood a flat area, colour line art or fill a selection with a pattern.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+G to cycle from the Gradient tool).

parameters.name: Fill
parameters.description: Foreground or Pattern.

parameters.name: Tolerance
parameters.description: Colour range filled around the clicked pixel.

parameters.name: Contiguous / All Layers
parameters.description: Restrict to the connected region; sample the composite.

parameters.name: Anti-alias
parameters.description: Softens the fill boundary by one pixel.

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+G until the Paint Bucket is active, Tolerance 32, Contiguous on.
2. Click inside a closed region of line art to flood it with the foreground colour.
tools.notes: Alt+Backspace fills a whole layer or selection with the foreground colour; Ctrl+Backspace fills with the background colour - usually faster than the tool.

tools.name: 3D Material Drop Tool (legacy)
tools.description: Part of Photoshop's discontinued 3D feature set: it dropped a material preset onto a face of a 3D mesh, sharing the G toolbar slot with the Gradient and Paint Bucket tools. Adobe deprecated Photoshop 3D from the 22.x releases and removed the 3D workspace in version 24, so on Photoshop 2025 (v26) this tool and the 3D menu are no longer present.
tools.usage: Historically: Toolbar (Shift+G to cycle) with a 3D layer active. Not available in Photoshop 2025.
tools.example:
Legacy workflow (Photoshop 22 and earlier):
1. 3D > New 3D Extrusion from Selected Layer.
2. Press Shift+G until the 3D Material Drop tool is active.
3. Pick a material preset from the options bar and click a face of the mesh.
tools.notes: Catalogued for completeness when working with old documents and tutorials. Use Adobe Substance 3D or Dimension for current 3D workflows.

tools.name: Blur Tool
tools.description: Softens detail wherever you paint by locally averaging pixels. Used sparingly for smoothing a harsh edge, knocking back a distracting texture or easing a composite seam. Strength controls how quickly the blur builds.
tools.usage: Toolbar (R slot fly-out; the Blur, Sharpen and Smudge tools have no single-key shortcut of their own).

parameters.name: Strength
parameters.description: 0-100%; keep it low (10-25%) and build up gradually.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Normal, Darken, Lighten, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity.

parameters.name: Sample All Layers
parameters.description: Blurs based on the composite of all visible layers.

tools.example:
1. Select the Blur tool from the toolbar fly-out, Strength 20%.
2. Paint along the hard edge where a pasted object meets the background to soften the join.
tools.notes: Destructive. A duplicated layer with Gaussian Blur plus a mask gives far more control.

tools.name: Sharpen Tool
tools.description: Increases local contrast along edges where you paint, with a Protect Detail option that avoids the pixel artefacts the old implementation produced. Useful for a touch of extra bite on eyes, jewellery or product edges.
tools.usage: Toolbar (fly-out beside the Blur tool).

parameters.name: Strength
parameters.description: 0-100%; 10-20% is usually enough.

parameters.name: Protect Detail
parameters.description: Enhances detail while minimising pixelated artefacts.

tools.example:
1. Choose the Sharpen tool, Strength 15%, Protect Detail on, Sample All Layers on.
2. Add an empty layer and brush twice over the iris of each eye.

tools.name: Smudge Tool
tools.description: Pushes pixels in the direction of the stroke as if dragging a finger through wet paint. Used for blending hair strands into a background, smoothing gradients and painterly effects; Finger Painting smears with the foreground colour instead of the existing pixels.
tools.usage: Toolbar (fly-out beside the Blur tool).

parameters.name: Strength
parameters.description: How far the pixels are dragged (0-100%).

parameters.name: Finger Painting
parameters.description: Starts each stroke with the foreground colour.

parameters.name: Sample All Layers
parameters.description: Smudges using the composite image.

tools.example:
1. Choose the Smudge tool, Strength 60%, a small soft tip.
2. Drag outwards from the edge of the hair to pull individual strands into the new background.

tools.name: Dodge Tool
tools.description: Lightens pixels where you paint, restricted to shadows, midtones or highlights, emulating darkroom dodging. With Protect Tones enabled it preserves hue and avoids the colour shifts that plagued the legacy implementation.
tools.usage: Toolbar (O). Hold Alt while dodging to burn instead.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: Shadows, Midtones (default) or Highlights.

parameters.name: Exposure
parameters.description: Strength per stroke; 3-10% for retouching.

parameters.name: Protect Tones
parameters.description: Prevents hue and saturation shifts.

tools.example:
Non-destructive alternative:
1. Layer > New > Layer, Mode = Soft Light, tick "Fill with Soft-Light-neutral color (50% gray)".
2. Paint with a low-opacity white brush to dodge and black to burn.

Or press O, Range = Midtones, Exposure 5%, and brush over the areas to lift.

tools.name: Burn Tool
tools.description: Darkens pixels where you paint, the counterpart of the Dodge tool, with the same Range, Exposure and Protect Tones controls. Used to deepen shadows, add weight to edges and shape a subject's form.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+O to cycle from the Dodge tool). Hold Alt while burning to dodge.
tools.example:
1. Press Shift+O until the Burn tool is active, Range = Shadows, Exposure 8%, Protect Tones on.
2. Brush along the underside of the subject to deepen the contact shadow.
tools.notes: Burning at high exposure clips shadow detail irrecoverably; work on a duplicate layer or a 50% grey Soft Light layer instead.

tools.name: Sponge Tool
tools.description: Locally increases (Saturate) or decreases (Desaturate) colour saturation, or in Grayscale mode shifts contrast. Useful for taking the heat out of an over-saturated patch of skin or lifting a dull area of a product.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+O to cycle).

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Saturate or Desaturate.

parameters.name: Flow
parameters.description: Rate of change per stroke.

parameters.name: Vibrance
parameters.description: Protects already saturated colours from clipping.

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+O until the Sponge tool is active, Mode = Desaturate, Flow 20%, Vibrance on.
2. Brush over the red patch on the model's cheek until it matches the rest of the skin.

tools.name: Pen Tool
tools.description: Draws precise Bezier paths and vector shapes: click for corner points, click-drag for smooth points with direction handles. Paths can be converted to selections (Ctrl+Enter), stroked, used as vector masks, or drawn directly as shape layers. The most accurate cut-out method for hard-edged, man-made objects.
tools.usage: Toolbar (P). Options bar sets the mode: Path, Shape or Pixels. Ctrl+Enter converts the path to a selection.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Shape (creates a vector shape layer), Path (a work path only), Pixels (rasterised fill).

parameters.name: Path operations
parameters.description: Combine, Subtract Front Shape, Intersect, Exclude Overlapping Shapes.

parameters.name: Rubber Band
parameters.description: Previews the next segment as you move the cursor (gear menu).

parameters.name: Auto Add/Delete
parameters.description: Clicking on a segment adds a point; clicking a point removes it.

tools.example:
1. Press P, Mode = Path.
2. Click around a bottle, dragging on the curves to shape the handles; Alt+click a point to break its handles.
3. Click the first point to close, then Ctrl+Enter to load it as a selection and add a layer mask.

JSX: iterate paths with app.activeDocument.pathItems and call pathItem.makeSelection();

tools.name: Freeform Pen Tool
tools.description: Draws a path by dragging freehand; Photoshop fits Bezier points to the stroke afterwards. Its Magnetic option makes it snap to contrast edges like the Magnetic Lasso but produces an editable path rather than a selection.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+P to cycle from the Pen).

parameters.name: Curve Fit
parameters.description: 0.5-10 px tolerance - higher values create fewer, smoother anchor points.

parameters.name: Magnetic
parameters.description: Snaps the path to the nearest strong edge, with Width, Contrast and Frequency settings.

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+P until the Freeform Pen is active and tick Magnetic.
2. Trace around a high-contrast subject.
3. Switch to the Direct Selection tool (A) to tidy the anchor points, then Ctrl+Enter.

tools.name: Curvature Pen Tool
tools.description: A simplified pen that builds smooth curves from plain clicks: each new point re-shapes the neighbouring curve without touching direction handles, and double-clicking a point toggles it between smooth and corner. The easiest pen for people who find Bezier handles awkward.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+P to cycle).
tools.example:
1. Press Shift+P until the Curvature Pen is active, Mode = Shape.
2. Click three points along a curved edge - the curve forms automatically.
3. Double-click a point to make it a sharp corner; drag any point to reshape the path.

tools.name: Add / Delete Anchor Point and Convert Point Tools
tools.description: The path-editing trio in the Pen fly-out. Add Anchor Point inserts a point on an existing segment, Delete Anchor Point removes one while keeping the curve continuous, and Convert Point switches a point between smooth (with handles) and corner, or breaks a smooth point's handles so each side can be angled independently.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Pen fly-out). With the Pen tool active and Auto Add/Delete on, hovering a segment or point switches automatically; hold Alt for the Convert Point behaviour.
tools.example:
1. Draw a rough path with the Pen tool.
2. Click a segment with the Add Anchor Point tool to insert a control point.
3. Alt+drag the point's handle with the Convert Point tool to make one side of the curve sharp.

tools.name: Horizontal Type Tool
tools.description: Creates editable text: click for point type, drag a box for paragraph type, or click on a path/inside a closed shape for type on a path or area type. All character and paragraph formatting lives in the options bar and the Character/Paragraph panels, and the layer stays fully editable and resolution-independent.
tools.usage: Toolbar (T). Commit with Ctrl+Enter or the tick in the options bar; Esc cancels.

parameters.name: Font family / style / size
parameters.description: Set in the options bar or the Character panel.

parameters.name: Anti-aliasing
parameters.description: None, Sharp, Crisp, Strong, Smooth, plus macOS/Windows LCD variants.

parameters.name: Alignment / Colour
parameters.description: Left, centre, right; fill colour of the type layer.

parameters.name: Create warped text
parameters.description: Opens Warp Text (Arc, Flag, Bulge, ...).

tools.name: Vertical Type Tool
tools.description: Sets type running top-to-bottom in vertical columns, used for CJK typography and for vertical Latin display text. The Character panel adds vertical-specific controls such as tate-chu-yoko (horizontal-in-vertical) when East Asian options are enabled.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+T to cycle from the Horizontal Type tool).
tools.example:
1. Press Shift+T until the Vertical Type tool is active.
2. Click on the canvas and type; the characters stack downwards.
3. Type > Orientation > Horizontal converts an existing layer instead.
tools.notes: Enable Preferences > Type > Show Asian Text Options for full vertical typesetting controls.

tools.name: Horizontal / Vertical Type Mask Tools
tools.description: Create a pixel selection in the shape of the typed characters instead of an editable type layer. Used to fill or cut letterforms out of an image, or to make a text-shaped layer mask. The text is not editable once committed, so a real type layer plus a clipping mask is usually the better route.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+T to cycle). Commit with Ctrl+Enter to turn the red overlay into a selection.
tools.example:
1. Press Shift+T until the Horizontal Type Mask tool is active.
2. Click on a photo layer and type "SUMMER"; the canvas shows a red mask overlay.
3. Ctrl+Enter to get the selection, then Ctrl+J to copy the photo inside the letters to a new layer.

tools.name: Path Selection Tool
tools.description: Selects and moves whole paths, subpaths and shape layers (the black arrow). Combined with the path operations in the options bar it merges, subtracts, intersects and excludes shape components, and aligns or distributes them.
tools.usage: Toolbar (A). Shift+A cycles to the Direct Selection tool.

parameters.name: Select
parameters.description: Active Layers or All Layers - determines which shape layers can be picked.

parameters.name: Path operations
parameters.description: Combine Shapes, Subtract Front Shape, Intersect Shape Areas, Exclude Overlapping Shapes, Merge Shape Components.

parameters.name: Path alignment
parameters.description: Align and distribute selected subpaths.

tools.example:
1. Press A and click the circle inside a compound shape.
2. Set Path operations to Subtract Front Shape - the circle punches a hole in the square.
3. Choose Merge Shape Components to flatten the result into one path.

tools.name: Direct Selection Tool
tools.description: Selects and edits individual anchor points and direction handles (the white arrow), reshaping a curve without redrawing it. Marquee-drag to select several points, then nudge them with the arrow keys.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+A to cycle from the Path Selection tool). Hold Ctrl with the Pen tool active to switch temporarily.
tools.example:
1. Press Shift+A until the Direct Selection tool is active.
2. Click an anchor point on a shape layer and drag its direction handle to flatten the curve.
3. Drag a marquee around three points and press the Down arrow four times to nudge them.

tools.name: Rectangle Tool
tools.description: Draws vector rectangles and rounded rectangles as live shape layers whose fill, stroke, size and independent corner radii stay editable in the Properties panel. The foundation of UI mockups, buttons, cards and frames.
tools.usage: Toolbar (U). Shift+U cycles the shape tools. Hold Shift while dragging for a square, Alt to draw from the centre.

parameters.name: Fill / Stroke
parameters.description: Solid colour, gradient, pattern or none, with stroke width, alignment, cap, join and dash pattern.

parameters.name: W / H
parameters.description: Exact dimensions, with a link button to constrain the ratio.

parameters.name: Corner radius
parameters.description: One value for all corners or four independent radii, live-editable after drawing.

parameters.name: Path operations / Align Edges
parameters.description: Boolean combination with other shapes; snap the shape to whole pixels.

tools.example:
1. Press U, choose the Rectangle tool and set Fill to a solid colour and Stroke to none.
2. Drag a 320 x 48 px rectangle, or click the canvas to type exact dimensions.
3. In the Properties panel set the corner radius to 8 px.

tools.name: Ellipse, Triangle, Polygon and Line Tools
tools.description: The remaining geometric shape tools, all producing live, re-editable vector shape layers with the same fill/stroke controls as the Rectangle. Polygon supports a star ratio and rounded corners, and Line draws a thin rectangle with optional arrowheads.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+U cycles: Rectangle, Ellipse, Triangle, Polygon, Line, Custom Shape).

parameters.name: Ellipse
parameters.description: Hold Shift for a perfect circle, Alt to draw from the centre.

parameters.name: Triangle
parameters.description: Equilateral by default (hold Shift); corner radius is editable.

parameters.name: Polygon
parameters.description: Number of sides, Star Ratio (below 100% makes a star), Smooth Star Indents, corner radius.

parameters.name: Line
parameters.description: Weight in pixels; Arrowheads (Start/End, Width, Length, Concavity) live in the gear menu.

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+U until the Polygon tool is active.
2. In the options bar set Sides = 5 and Star Ratio = 50%.
3. Shift+drag to draw a symmetrical five-pointed star, then change the radius in Properties.

tools.name: Custom Shape Tool
tools.description: Draws any shape from the Shapes panel presets - arrows, banners, speech bubbles, symbols, plus the legacy shape libraries - as a vector shape layer. New presets are made with Edit > Define Custom Shape from any path, and .csh/shape groups can be imported.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+U to cycle). Pick a preset from the Shape menu in the options bar or from Window > Shapes.
tools.example:
1. Draw a path with the Pen tool and run Edit > Define Custom Shape.
2. Press Shift+U until the Custom Shape tool is active and select the new preset.
3. Shift+drag to place it at its original proportions.
tools.notes: Window > Shapes > panel menu > Legacy Shapes and More restores the pre-2020 shape sets.

tools.name: Hand Tool and Rotate View Tool
tools.description: The two canvas navigation tools. The Hand tool pans a zoomed-in document (hold the Space bar from any other tool for a temporary Hand). The Rotate View tool spins the canvas on screen without altering a single pixel, so you can paint or mask along an awkward angle comfortably; Reset View returns it to zero.
tools.usage: Hand: toolbar (H), or hold Space. Rotate View: toolbar (R); Esc or the Reset View button restores the original orientation.

parameters.name: Scroll All Windows
parameters.description: Pans every open document at once - useful when comparing two versions.

parameters.name: Rotation Angle
parameters.description: Numeric field in the options bar; Shift+drag snaps to 15 degree increments.

tools.example:
1. Zoom to 200%, hold Space and drag to pan to the eye.
2. Press R and drag to rotate the canvas 30 degrees so the eyelash runs horizontally.
3. Paint along the lash, then press Esc to reset the view.
tools.notes: Rotate View requires the graphics processor to be enabled in Preferences > Performance.

tools.name: Zoom Tool
tools.description: Changes the magnification of the document view. Scrubby Zoom lets you drag left/right to zoom smoothly; dragging a rectangle (with Scrubby Zoom off) zooms to that area. The options bar also holds the Fit Screen, Fill Screen and 100% buttons.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Z). Ctrl++ / Ctrl+- zoom in and out, Ctrl+0 fits the screen, Ctrl+1 shows 100%. Alt+scroll zooms with any tool when enabled in Preferences.

parameters.name: Scrubby Zoom
parameters.description: Drag right to zoom in, left to zoom out, continuously.

parameters.name: Resize Windows to Fit
parameters.description: Grows or shrinks the document window with the zoom level in floating-window mode.

parameters.name: Zoom All Windows
parameters.description: Applies the zoom to every open document.

tools.example:
1. Press Z and drag right across the canvas to zoom into the detail.
2. Alt+click to zoom back out.
3. Ctrl+0 to fit the whole image on screen again.
